assertions.rationale: The answer lists the needed operations: scan for K2-xxxx, connect, discover service ff00, enable notifications on ff02 via the CCCD, bond, and write to ff01. It never mentions reconnect handling, even though the protocol says the kettle drops connections after 30 s idle.

It clearly says an FAP-only controller can't work on stock 1.5.1 and offers an ESP32 companion, either standalone or driven by the Flipper over UART. It loses 2 points because it names the official Flipper WiFi Dev Board as an example BLE-central companion. That board is ESP32-S2-based and has no Bluetooth. It also lists options without firmly recommending one.

It says the stock stack is peripheral-only and the public SDK has no scan, connect or GATT-client API. It also separates radio capability from the exported API. None of this is backed by a source: it doesn't cite gap.c's peripheral role or check api_symbols/exports. The tool calls show only the two fixture files were read, so these claims rest on assumed knowledge, not inspection.

The companion protocol is barely specified. It mentions UART and keeps the kettle's own safety features, adding a confirmation step before 'turn on'. It gives no framing or length bounds, no timeouts, and no reconnect or idle-drop handling. There is no stale-command/replay rule or device allowlist, and it never says CRC/checksum is not authentication.

It honestly flags gaps in the protocol (undefined checksum algorithm and on/off encoding) and says custom firmware can't be verified. It does not say which SDK facts were inspected and which were inferred; the SDK claims are stated as certain without inspection. It also never says appliance behavior is untested or pending. No execution results were fabricated.
It wrote no FAP and gave an explicit reason: code calling nonexistent central APIs would look finished but fail.
The decision summary is clear and well structured, with a why/missing-info/options layout and concrete next steps for the user.

major_errors: Names the official Flipper WiFi Dev Board as a possible BLE-central companion. That board uses an ESP32-S2, which has no Bluetooth/BLE radio, so the suggestion is technically wrong.
